title: Acts 9:20–31
context: Saul immediately proclaims in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God, astonishing those who knew why he came. He grows stronger and confounds the Jews of Damascus, who plot to kill him, but the disciples lower him over the wall in a basket. In Jerusalem the disciples fear him until Barnabas vouches for him. He speaks boldly and debates the Hellenists, who also try to kill him, so the believers send him to Tarsus. The church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria has peace and multiplies.

verses.text: Immediately in the synagogues he proclaimed the Christ, that he is the Son of God.
verses.arminianNotes: Saul immediately proclaims Jesus as the Son of God. Arminian readers see a complete reversal expressed in bold witness.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the new heart producing new speech.

verses.text: All who heard him were amazed, and said, “Isn’t this he who in Jerusalem made havoc of those who called on this name? And he had come here intending to bring them bound before the chief priests!”
verses.arminianNotes: All who hear are amazed that the persecutor now preaches. Arminian commentators see a testimony that cannot be explained apart from God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see grace displayed in the most unlikely convert.

verses.text: But Saul increased more in strength, and confounded the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.
verses.arminianNotes: Saul grows stronger and confounds the Jews by proving Jesus is the Christ. Arminian readers see Saul using his learning in service of the gospel.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God turning Saul’s training toward his purposes.

verses.text: When many days were fulfilled, the Jews conspired together to kill him,
verses.arminianNotes: After many days the Jews plot to kill him. Arminian expositors see the persecutor becoming the persecuted.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the suffering foretold in 9:16 beginning.

verses.text: but their plot became known to Saul. They watched the gates both day and night that they might kill him,
verses.arminianNotes: The plot becomes known, and they watch the gates day and night. Arminian readers see God giving warning.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see providence protecting his servant.

verses.text: but his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
verses.arminianNotes: His disciples lower him through the wall in a basket. Arminian commentators note the humble escape, which Paul recalls in 2 Corinthians 11:33.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see God preserving Saul through ordinary means.

verses.text: When Saul had come to Jerusalem, he tried to join himself to the disciples; but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
verses.arminianNotes: In Jerusalem the disciples are afraid and doubt his conversion. Arminian readers see understandable caution.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see that genuine conversion sometimes needs time and witness to be recognized.

verses.text: But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles, and declared to them how he had seen the Lord on the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.
verses.arminianNotes: Barnabas brings him to the apostles and tells his story. Arminian expositors see Barnabas living up to his name as an encourager.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see God using one believer to vouch for another.

verses.text: He was with them entering into Jerusalem,
verses.arminianNotes: Saul moves freely with them in Jerusalem. Arminian readers see him accepted into fellowship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the church receiving him as one of its own.

verses.text: preaching boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He spoke and disputed against the Hellenists, but they were seeking to kill him.
verses.arminianNotes: He preaches boldly and debates the Hellenists, who seek to kill him. Arminian commentators see Saul engaging the same group that opposed Stephen.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see Saul taking up Stephen’s work.

verses.text: When the brothers knew it, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
verses.arminianNotes: The brothers take him to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Arminian readers see the community protecting him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see a season of preparation before his wider mission.

verses.text: So the assemblies throughout all Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and were built up. They were multiplied, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.
verses.arminianNotes: The church has peace, is built up, walks in the fear of the Lord and the comfort of the Spirit, and multiplies. Arminian expositors see growth that follows faithful living.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the Spirit’s comfort and the fear of God sustaining and enlarging the church.
